sections.paragraph: Paxlovid is indicated for mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults at high risk of severe disease. Trials of longer courses for established Long COVID have not demonstrated the expected symptom advantage. The co-packaged tablets have separate roles: nirmatrelvir interrupts viral protein processing and ritonavir slows nirmatrelvir breakdown. That antiviral action underlies the acute-infection indication, which is restricted to adults at high risk of progression. Research in established Long COVID asks a different question about symptoms continuing after the initial illness. STOP-PASC tested 15 days rather than the labeled five-day acute course. Both STOP-PASC and RECOVER-VITAL reported no significant primary symptom advantage in their studied Long COVID populations. The approved acute use therefore does not establish effectiveness for persistent symptoms or validate extending treatment for that purpose.

sections.paragraph: Early treatment of high-risk acute COVID-19 and treatment of established Long COVID are different uses. STOP-PASC and RECOVER-VITAL did not find significant primary symptom benefit from their longer courses. For acute infection, the prescribing information specifies adults at high risk of progression to hospitalization or death. The persistent-symptom trials should be read separately from that approved role. STOP-PASC did not find significant pooled symptom improvement after its 15-day course. RECOVER-VITAL also reported no significant primary benefit in the cognitive, autonomic and exercise-intolerance groups it studied. These findings concern the specific longer courses and selected symptom groups, rather than proving that every proposed viral-persistence explanation is impossible. They do show that the rationale for extending antiviral exposure did not produce the expected primary clinical advantage in those comparisons.

sections.paragraph: Naltrexone has established addiction-treatment uses. Repurposing evidence differs by condition: an uncontrolled Long COVID cohort reported improvements, while a larger fibromyalgia trial did not show a significant pain benefit. Its established action is competitive blockade of opioid receptors, and the oral tablet label covers alcohol dependence and blockade of exogenous opioids. Repurposing studies do not all test the same dose or outcome. The Long COVID cohort followed 59 patients without a randomized comparison. The fibromyalgia trial tested 6 mg daily, while the compulsive-behavior trial used 50 mg daily. A separate ME/CFS experiment measured a calcium-permeable channel in isolated immune cells. Those distinctions matter because patient symptom changes, a randomized pain comparison and a laboratory channel result provide different kinds of information about the investigated uses.

sections.paragraph: A Long COVID cohort reported improved fatigue, post-exertional symptoms and sleep, but its uncontrolled design cannot distinguish a drug effect from other changes. Fibromyalgia pain did not improve significantly more than with placebo in the 99-woman trial; compulsive-behavior findings varied by the outcome measure. The 59-patient Long COVID report associated treatment with fewer symptoms and improved functional status, but provides no placebo-adjusted response estimate. In fibromyalgia, the 12-week between-group pain difference was -0.34 points, with a confidence interval from -0.95 to 0.27, so a significant pain advantage was not demonstrated. In the 73-man compulsive sexual behavior trial, clinical interviews favored active treatment while self-report questionnaires did not separate it from placebo. That trial did not study persistent genital arousal disorder or genitopelvic dysesthesia. Its behavioral findings therefore cannot establish relief of persistent unwanted genital sensations in those different conditions.

sections.paragraph: Oral ivermectin is used for strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis. A higher-dose COVID-19 trial did not speed recovery; the cancer studies discussed here are preclinical. Its established antiparasitic action involves glutamate-gated chloride channels in susceptible parasites. The COVID-19 and cancer questions go beyond those oral indications and need their own evidence. ACTIV-6 directly tested recovery in patients using a maximum target dose of 600 micrograms/kg daily for six days, without finding improvement. The ovarian, glioblastoma, breast and colorectal investigations measured pathways, growth or other responses in experimental systems. They do not supply an estimate of cancer survival or symptom benefit in patients. The ivermectin-sorafenib liver-cancer report is retracted and excluded, so it must not contribute support for an efficacy claim.

sections.paragraph: Guanfacine extended release is an ADHD medicine. Its Long COVID evidence includes a small uncontrolled series using combination treatment. The Intuniv product is an extended-release formulation, with an established ADHD indication rather than a Long COVID indication. Guanfacine stimulates central alpha-2A receptors and can lower blood pressure and heart rate, although the label says the mechanism of ADHD benefit is unknown. The Long COVID series combined it with N-acetylcysteine to investigate cognitive symptoms. Eight of twelve participants reported improvement, while four stopped, including two with hypotension or dizziness. Without placebo or a single-drug comparison, that report cannot isolate guanfacine's contribution or establish how commonly cognitive improvement would occur with treatment in a broader Long COVID population. Immediate-release and extended-release guanfacine are not interchangeable milligram for milligram.

Its initial nighttime dose and increase if tolerated should therefore remain separate from the extended-release product's labeled ADHD titration. sections.paragraph: Rituximab is used in specified B-cell cancers and autoimmune diseases. Its vitiligo evidence includes an uncontrolled five-person pilot. The established action is depletion of CD20-positive B cells, a target relevant to its specified cancer and autoimmune indications. Three showed clear clinical and histological improvement, one slight improvement and one no change. Without a control group, this does not establish an average treatment effect, durability beyond follow-up or a validated retreatment schedule. Clinical appearance and skin-biopsy changes were recorded in the same five participants, so they should not be counted as separate clinical trials. The three clear improvements, one slight improvement and one unchanged case describe the range observed after a single infusion. They do not establish what would have happened without treatment or what proportion of a broader vitiligo population would benefit. The report also cannot show whether improvement persists beyond six months or whether further infusions are useful. These limits leave clinical evidence Low and keep the autoimmune rationale distinct from a demonstrated, durable, comparatively estimated effect on pigmentation.

sections.paragraph: The clearest distinction is between periodontal therapy and acute COVID-19. Low-dose doxycycline is an adjunct to mechanical periodontal treatment; PRINCIPLE did not support routine doxycycline for community COVID-19. sections.paragraph: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. Physical or mental effort can cause a delayed worsening of symptoms. Naltrexone research has examined altered signaling in natural-killer immune cells as one possible treatment target. The selected treatment research should be distinguished from the illness definition. A natural-killer-cell study examined TRPM3 channel currents in nine people already taking naltrexone and nine healthy controls. It did not randomize ME/CFS patients to treatment or measure recovery. Three separate patient-compiled case histories described variable symptoms during naltrexone use, including one account of improved pain and sleep without improved function. Those observations do not establish that one immune pathway explains the whole illness. The condition's reduced activity and delayed post-exertional worsening remain clinical concerns that a cell measurement alone cannot resolve.

sections.paragraph: Treatment-resistant depression describes continuing depressive illness despite adequate treatment attempts. Its symptoms can include loss of pleasure, motivation and daily function as well as persistent low mood. Pramipexole, originally used for movement disorders, has been studied as an addition to existing antidepressants. The PAX-D investigation concerns treatment-resistant unipolar depression, rather than all depressive conditions or a replacement for existing antidepressants. Its augmentation design added pramipexole to ongoing treatment and compared that addition with placebo. At 12 weeks, depressive symptoms improved more with active augmentation, but adverse effects also led to more treatment stops. This establishes a specific benefit and tolerability question. It does not determine whether pramipexole alone is effective, whether the same balance applies to bipolar depression or how it ranks against another active augmentation option. The dopamine rationale addresses reward and motivation without identifying one biochemical cause of every participant's illness.

sections.paragraph: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. It can damage bone and interfere with healthy blood-cell production. Thalidomide is an example of repurposing that reached an approved cancer indication. That supportive-care endpoint does not test aspirin's antimyeloma activity. Keeping established cancer treatment, experimental tumor effects and prevention of treatment-associated clots distinct makes the intervention landscape clearer without suggesting that the selected sources are a complete treatment review.

sections.paragraph: Sarcopenia involves declining muscle strength and function, often with reduced muscle mass. Difficulty rising from a chair, slower walking and increased falls can threaten independence. Resistance activity and adequate nutrition are central to preserving muscle health. This makes the endpoint important when evaluating a repurposed medicine: walking performance, strength and muscle size are related but different measures. MET-PREVENT tested metformin in 72 older adults with prefrailty or frailty and found no detectable walking-speed advantage over four months. MASTERS instead examined adaptation during progressive resistance training and found smaller muscle-size gains with metformin; differences in strength gains were not significant. These studies challenge a general assumption that improving metabolism necessarily improves muscle aging. Their selected populations and interventions should remain distinct, with physical function assessed directly rather than inferred solely from a change in muscle mass.

sections.paragraph: Healthy aging includes maintaining physical, mental and cognitive function, independence and quality of life. Longevity research also asks whether interventions can extend lifespan; these are related but distinct goals. The selected human trials address narrower questions within healthy aging. A secondary body-composition change in a small human subgroup cannot establish longer life or define a general anti-aging treatment benefit.

sections.paragraph: Tadalafil inhibits PDE5, an enzyme involved in smooth-muscle relaxation. It is used for erectile dysfunction, urinary symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia and, under a separate indication, pulmonary arterial hypertension. Cialis and Adcirca contain the same active ingredient but cover different labeled uses and regimens. The pulmonary indication is specifically WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension, so it does not include every type of pulmonary hypertension. Repurposing research has also examined secondary Raynaud phenomenon, where reduced finger circulation produces a separate vascular question. Two small crossover studies reached conflicting symptom findings. One tested an add-on to existing vasodilators and observed fewer attacks and improved ulcer healing; the other did not show a symptom advantage over placebo. Thus the vascular rationale and established indications provide context, while Raynaud benefit remains a separate clinical question.
